Hi @damianobarbati ,

Thanks for asking, indeed I had to pull out 2 constants from the fingerprint computing to bypass an issue that was giving _different_ fingerprints for the _same_ browser depending on the way the new window / or now tab had been opened (new window, vs new tab, vs window.open, vs browser already launched or new launch). 
I'm working on Mac OSX and this issue was occurring on Chrome and Firefox (probably it was both). See my commit message at the time I did the change:
`Removed plugins and mimeTypes const from the fingerprint as they might differ onto the same browser depending how it was opened`
Hope this helps!

@8ctopus thanks for sharing this, all of your assumptions look correct to me:

> every browser has its own fingerprints
> all fingerprints remain the same after clearing the browser cache

Yes, the fingerprint identifies uniquely the browser.
If your goal is to identity the device (any browser, given your use cases) then you can try removing the `userAgent` [here](<https://github.com/damianobarbati/get-browser-fingerprint/blob/main/src/index.js#L63>): I'm afraid several bits may change anyway in the several factors considered when computing the fingerprint causing a different hash for each browser (I didn't test this, but give it a try and let me know!).

> the hardware only fingerprint is unaltered in private mode, all others change.
Also true, I can't remember now which factors are impacted in the private mode where vendors are try to prevent fingerprinting techniques.

@NeaByteLab I prefer to:
- keep the FP as short as possible
- avoid the use of crypto.subtle requiring SSL (I know that on localhost you can use it anyway, but you won't be able to test from your smartphone to local machina running a webserver - eg 192.168.1.10 - you would need ssl tunnels)
- the missing semicolon on statements suggest no biome was run maybe?

Got it.

I reverted to a short 8-char hex fingerprint and removed crypto.subtle entirely (pure JS MurmurHash3), so it works over plain HTTP/LAN. Also ran Biome (pnpm lint) and tests are green.
